description:
## What

Thread `AiaFetcher` through `pkix-chain` as the third trust-domain callback alongside `SignatureVerifier` and `RevocationChecker`. Re-export `pkix_aia::AiaFetcher` and `pkix_aia::NoAiaFetcher` from pkix-chain so callers see the full seam in one crate.

## API shape

`Verifier` struct (from PKIX-gsd9) gains a third generic parameter:

```rust
pub struct Verifier<'a, V: SignatureVerifier, R: RevocationChecker, A: AiaFetcher> {
    anchors: &'a [TrustAnchor],
    policy: &'a ValidationPolicy,
    verifier: &'a V,
    revocation: &'a R,
    aia: &'a A,
}

impl<'a, V, R, A> Verifier<'a, V, R, A> { /* verify_one, verify_batch */ }
```

`verify_chain` free function gets an extra parameter (or a builder, depending on PKIX-gsd9 final shape):

```rust
pub fn verify_chain(
    chain:      &[Certificate],
    anchors:    &[TrustAnchor],
    policy:     &ValidationPolicy,
    verifier:   &impl SignatureVerifier,
    revocation: &impl RevocationChecker,
    aia:        &impl AiaFetcher,    // NEW
) -> Result<ValidatedPath, Error>;
```

A `verify_chain_default()` convenience uses `NoAiaFetcher` to preserve the existing "no online lookups" default behavior.

## Chain-build flow with AiaFetcher

Before path-build (pkix-path-builder), inspect the caller-supplied chain:

1. If chain is complete (root reachable from leaf via in-chain issuers), no AIA fetch needed.
2. If chain is missing an intermediate: extract AIA URIs from the cert whose issuer is missing (use `extract_aia_http_urls` helper, possibly migrated to pkix-aia).
3. Call `aia.batch_fetch(&uris)` — try all URIs, pick first that returns a valid Certificate matching the needed issuer DN + SKI.
4. Add fetched cert to the candidate pool; pass to path-builder.
5. If all AIA fetches fail: return chain-build error wrapping the AiaError.

Loop: a fetched intermediate may itself have a missing issuer. Cap recursion depth (e.g. 5) to prevent unbounded fetching.

## Error type

`pkix_chain::Error` gains new variants:

```rust
pub enum Error {
    // ... existing variants ...
    AiaFetchFailed { uri: String, error: AiaError },
    AiaChainBuildFailed { reason: String },
}
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `Verifier` gains third generic `A: AiaFetcher`
- [ ] `verify_chain` signature includes `&impl AiaFetcher` parameter
- [ ] `verify_chain_default` uses `NoAiaFetcher`
- [ ] Chain with missing intermediate validates when AiaFetcher provides it
- [ ] Chain with missing intermediate fails cleanly when AiaFetcher returns FetchingDisabled (no panic, no infinite loop)
- [ ] Recursion cap (default 5 levels of AIA fetches) enforced
- [ ] Existing tests still pass (use NoAiaFetcher where they previously had no AIA callback)
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry on pkix-chain noting the API addition
- [ ] AGENTS.md `pkix-chain` description updated to mention AiaFetcher as the third trust-domain callback

## Out of scope

- Caching the AIA fetcher results (caller wraps with caching layer)
- LDAP fetcher (pkix-aia-ldap could be a separate adapter crate; file as a follow-up if demand surfaces)
- Pre-fetching all AIA URIs even for complete chains

## Cross-references

- PKIX-zkjb (parent)
- PKIX-zkjb.3 (trait def)
- PKIX-zkjb.4 (NoAiaFetcher default)
- PKIX-gsd9 (Verifier struct shape, recently shipped)
title: Integrate AiaFetcher into pkix-chain Verifier and verify_chain entry points
